correctness.rationale: Independence forces all positive labels into one part. A zero left in that same part would have no positive neighbor, so the entire chosen part must be positive; zeros outside are defended exactly when at least one chosen vertex is labeled 2. This gives the displayed binomial summand for each part. The reconstruction argument is triangular in descending part size because the coefficient at degree twice the largest part size counts precisely the largest parts. I independently compared the literal definition to the classifier on every ordered multipartite composition through order seven, totaling 164682 labelings, and matched the polynomial histograms for all such profiles; the packaged verifier extends its own census through order nine.
risks: The disconnected one-part edgeless case is intentionally excluded.

value.rationale: Although the feasibility proof is short, the exact all-function polynomial is a natural invariant of a canonical graph family and has a nontrivial reconstruction consequence: within connected complete multipartite graphs it determines the graph up to isomorphism. That makes the result more than a routine minimum calculation.
risks: The result remains specialized to complete multipartite graphs.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph, an independent Roman dominating function is obtained exactly by choosing one whole part, labeling all of its vertices by 1 or 2 with at least one 2, and assigning 0 elsewhere; hence the stated weight enumerator follows and uniquely recovers the multiset of part sizes.
limitations: No algorithmic or complexity claim for general graphs.
